THE FINDING -- THE NIGHTLY SESSION FAILED 14 OF 40 TIMES AND NOTHING EVER RE-RAN IT. Mined selflearn.log over 07-24..08-31 (the era where 'Session ended (exit N)' exists): 26 ok, 14 failed = 65% success. Cause breakdown: 7 usage limits whose reset time was HOURS away, 4 infrastructure (missing binary, 60-min timeout, a shell typo), 3 limits resetting next day.

CORRECTION to the 08-31 note, which ranked 'no alert exists for a missed session' as item 1: an alert DOES exist -- self_improve.sh has DM'd the owner on every non-zero exit since it was written, and all three of 08-28/29/30 exited 1. Detection was never the gap. RECOVERY was. A detector tells you the bot ran unsupervised; a retry means it didn't.

FIXED (self_improve.sh) -- automatic same-day retries. 'session limit' always resets between 02:10 and 04:00 UTC and 'weekly limit' at 14:00, so cron now runs --retry at 04:30 and --retry-last at 15:00. Replayed against the historical record: 7 of the 14 lost nights would have been recovered (65% -> 82% session success), including 08-29 and 08-30, which would have cut the recent 4-day unsupervised run to 1 day. A human already proved the mechanism by hand -- on 07-26 the 02:00 run died on a spend limit and a manual 04:41 rerun succeeded.

The retries are safe because of one guard: a retry is a NO-OP once a success marker (.last_session) carries today's date, so on a normal night it costs one stat() and writes nothing. It also doubles as the missing-session detector -- it keys on 'did today succeed', not on 'did 02:00 report a failure', so it fires even if cron never ran the 02:00 job at all. Alarm-fatigue budget respected: the 04:30 retry sends NO DM on failure (it would be a second notice about a failure already reported at 02:00); only the final 15:00 attempt escalates, with a distinct 'no nightly session completed today'.

THREE BUGS FOUND BY WRITING THE TEST, not by reading the code:
(1) The escalation case matched 'retry-last' while the argument is '--retry-last', so the end-of-day alert would have silently never fired -- the exact class of bug the whole change exists to prevent.
(2) self_improve.sh pins PATH at line 7, which DISCARDS any PATH a caller sets. The first version of the test redirected PATH to a stub claude, the pin threw it away, and a REAL nightly session launched and orphaned to ppid=1, running unsupervised with acceptEdits alongside this one. Killed by PID; no damage (git status clean, strategy2.py md5 unchanged). Added an explicit SELF_IMPROVE_BIN_PREFIX seam, plus process-group kill and a source pre-flight in the test so an escape aborts instead of running.
(3) The failure detector grepped the WHOLE transcript for 'hit your session/weekly limit'. Tonight's own report discusses those strings at length, so a SUCCESSFUL session would have been scored as failed and triggered a redundant 04:30 run. Scoped to the first 200 bytes, where a CLI refusal is the entire output. An instrument must not match its own output.

ALSO FIXED: the failure DM interpolated raw session output into a parse_mode=HTML send without tg.esc(). Harmless for 'You've hit your session limit', fatal for a traceback containing '<urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection object at 0x...>' -- Telegram rejects it as bad entities and the alert is lost precisely when the failure is interesting. Same class as the 08-07 HTML sweep.

ALSO FIXED: self_improve.sh now re-execs from an immutable snapshot of itself. Bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset, so editing this file while it runs makes the live shell resume mid-token -- and the session it launches edits files in this repo, including this one. Tonight's edits were made to the running script; the tail holds no destructive command, so the worst case was a lost log append.
